AIRSIDE Kai Tak · Opening KOL Experience · October 2026 · AGENCY BRIEF

SEOUL, BY HAND

One goal: when Hong Kong thinks K-fashion, it thinks MLB.
Not a ribbon — a cart on the concourse, a needle running all afternoon, and twelve people who leave wearing something that did not exist that morning.

6 Oct 2026 — tentative 12 KOLs 1 trolley — the SEOUL STAND, coffee + tea #SeoulByHand #MLBHK
IN-STORE INFLUENCER EVENT — AIRSIDE, KAI TAK · AGENCY BRIEF
StoreMLB AIRSIDE (M24), Kai Tak, Hong Kong — 72.4 m² total, 58.1 m² sales floor
ConceptSEOUL, BY HAND — when Hong Kong thinks K-fashion, it thinks MLB. Nothing on the day is watched; everything is made.
Event date6 October 2026 (Tuesday) — tentative
Objective
  1. Strengthen MLB's K-fashion standing in Hong Kong.
  2. Embrace the team-diversity concept — the league across the floor, not a single club.
  3. Open the door with something the concourse stops for.
Content
  1. 12 creators, each on site two hours.
  2. The SEOUL STAND — one trolley at the storefront, coffee and six Korean teas, three stools.
  3. The gift: CREW TEA COLLECTION — six Korean teas in a satin pouch, one set each.
  4. Store tour video and asset usage.
Run of day
12:00 – 13:30
Set-up — cart, drink caddy, mirror decal, charm bar, stock the machine
14:00 – 16:00
Influencer window — arrive, drink, park the cup, fit check, stitch, charm
16:00 – 17:00
Store tour video, product capture, group frame at the stand
17:00
End — the cart and caddy strike, the mirror decal and the machine stay

Proposed. The creators' availability sets the final date.

01

Three experiences — not three photo ops

Every minute is something they do with their hands or their mouth. Three experiences, all on assets we already own.

☕
THEY TASTE
K-café and Korean tea

One trolley, the SEOUL STAND: coffee, six Korean teas, three stools. A place to sit in the middle of a mall — and not one square metre of shop floor.

🧵
THEY STITCH
embroidery, live on the cap

Minutes at the machine and the cap belongs to one person only. They watch the needle put their own mark on it.

🪢
THEY TIE
the Korean knot, tied by hand

The gift is a norigae — the Korean knot worn on hanbok for centuries. They tie it themselves and hang it on their own bag. A giveaway becomes twenty minutes of craft.

04

Five stations, drawn

Every stop is an object, not an adjective. Three of the five already stand in the shop. What we add is a cart, a caddy and a sheet of vinyl.

01 · THE SEOUL STAND

The approved barrow: pitched sign board, six cap marks, drop-leaf ledge and three high stools. The full elevation is in §04C.

02 · THE DRINK CADDY

A brushed stainless tray — twelve holes, cut handles both ends — on a slim stand at the door. Cups go in it before anyone steps inside, sleeves facing out.

03 · THE FIT CHECK

The existing W 1,250 mirror, dressed in applied vinyl: a scatter of team stickers top and bottom with the AIRSIDE plate at eye level, so a full-length shot lands inside the frame however she stands.

04 · THE STITCH

The machine we already own, on a bench with the thread stand beside it. The cap sits in the frame with the 40 × 35 mm side panel under the needle — worked standing, no stool.

05 · THE CHARM BAR

A brushed-steel hang rack — knots on the top rail, tassels below. The six team logo charms stay in the shelf box with the nickel findings, cord and beads — nine compartments, nothing printed, no signage.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY BUY

Three of the five are already standing in the shop.

The machine, the mirror and the display run are fixtures. We add a cart, a caddy and a sheet of vinyl — and the day is built.

04B

The AIRSIDE mark

The graphic is what makes this store different. Two marks — one reads Hong Kong, one reads Seoul, and they never compete on the same cap. Flat colour, inside the 40 × 35 mm cap side panel.

A

A · TWO FLOWERS

Two blooms, each carrying the other's colour.

B

B · TWO LANTERNS

Seoul's blue lantern beside Hong Kong's red one.

Two marks, one rotation. Both go on the machine on the day — the creator picks which one goes on their cap.

04C

The F&B — one trolley, the SEOUL STAND

One trolley. Coffee on one half, Korean tea on the other, six team marks across the sign board, three high stools under a drop-leaf ledge. A barrow, not a counter — painted body, one big wordmark, oak top with a folding drop-leaf, pitched roof, one oversized wheel. It parks at the storefront with the whole F&B on it.

↔ SWIPE TO SEE THE WHOLE DRAWING

One plain black cup, six knit sleeves on a rail. She picks her team and slides it on. One cup SKU — and the sleeve is the only part that leaves with her.

↔ SWIPE TO SEE THE WHOLE DRAWING

Tea half: display, tea set, brewing in the counter. Coffee half: self-service machine, disposable cups. Drink racks and the sleeve rail along the top, six team marks on the sign board, three stools under the drop-leaf. One server, install and dismantle included. Mirror stickers and insurance sit in the same line.

04D

The gift — the CREW TEA COLLECTION

Twelve sets — the cart's tea menu, to take home. Six sachets, six team marks in each, 6 designs × 12 = 72 bags.

↔ SWIPE TO SEE THE WHOLE DRAWING

The packaging. A navy satin bokjumeoni — the Korean lucky pouch — with the six sachets inside.

REFERENCE PHOTO

Navy satin, gathered top, gold cord — the piece we are matching.

↔ SWIPE TO SEE THE WHOLE DRAWING

One gift, one pouch. Reusable, and it carries the Korean story on its own. One small MLB on the face and nothing else — the six teas do the rest.
